eccentric

ik-SEN-trik — literally 'off-center'; an eccentric person just doesn't orbit the same way everyone else does. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Eccentric is unconventional and a little strange, especially in behavior or appearance.

The eccentric millionaire kept a pet llama in his living room and answered his front door dressed as a pirate.

Example

A brilliant but eccentric chemistry teacher insists on wearing a different colored lab coat every day of the week, keeps a collection of over two hundred rubber ducks on his desk, and always ends class by singing the periodic table instead of just reciting it.

Being delightfully odd and unconventional in a harmless way is what makes the teacher eccentric. Unlike 'crazy,' which can suggest something is wrong, eccentric usually has a fond, admiring tone about someone's quirks.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unconventional: Unconventional simply means not following what is normal or expected — a neutral report that something is different. Eccentric adds personality and tone: an eccentric person is unconventional in odd, memorable ways, usually described with fondness or amusement rather than plain fact.

peculiar: Peculiar means strange or unusual, often with a faint note of unease — a peculiar smell, a peculiar silence. Eccentric is warmer: it describes a person's harmless, often endearing oddness, not something vaguely off or suspicious.

idiosyncratic: Idiosyncratic means distinctive to one particular person — a habit or style that is theirs alone, whether or not it is strange at all. Eccentric stresses oddness measured against what is normal; idiosyncratic stresses ownership, a way of doing things that belongs to one person only.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

conventional: following what is normal or expected

ordinary: not unusual or special; normal

Where it sits · how far from normal it strays

quirky → eccentric → bizarre

quirky vs. eccentric: Quirky is a lighter, more affectionate word than eccentric — quirky often describes small, charming habits, while eccentric can describe a whole unconventional lifestyle or personality.

bizarre vs. eccentric: Bizarre can feel more extreme than eccentric: eccentric usually has a fond, harmless tone, but bizarre suggests something genuinely strange or hard to explain.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ec- (ek-): out of (Greek)

root — -centr-: center (Greek (kentron))

suffix — -ic: having the nature of (Greek (-ikos))

Put it together: Greek ek- ('out of') plus kentron ('center') plus the adjective ending -ic ('having the nature of') builds 'off-center.' Someone eccentric literally doesn't orbit the same conventional path as everyone else.

Use the root in a new word: concentrate: Half the physics quiz turned out to be about centrifugal force, and she had studied the wrong chapter.
